place.source_title: Fire Barn No. 5, 533 Saint Charles Street

brief: Two-storey neighbourhood fire station of about 1904: buff brick with red-brick quoins and trim, a pair of big red engine doors under round arches, a bracketed cornice, and a hipped roof crowned by a square hose-drying cupola; the police substation shares the side door. A bell mounted on a brick base out front.

facade.notes: Elgin IL Fire Barn No. 5 (c.1904): a two-storey buff-brick firehouse with red-brick quoins, a pair of red arched engine doors and a pedestrian door, a second-floor canted bay under a hipped roof with a belvedere (hose-drying/lookout); now a museum, under big oaks

why.note: the neighbourhood firehouse: engine doors on the ground, the crew's rooms above, a tower to dry hoses; spaced so a team could reach every house in a few minutes
